items.summary: Target delivered impressive Q3 results with comp sales of +5.6% beating estimates, while Walmart's results were merely adequate with decelerating comp growth of +2.9% and disappointing guidance. Despite Walmart's premium 40X valuation and defensive positioning, it has underperformed this year. items.title: WMT Q3 Earnings Call Takeaways as Sales and Profit Outlooks Rise
items.summary: Walmart raised its fiscal 2027 sales and profit guidance following strong Q3 results, with global e-commerce sales surging 17% and revenues climbing 5.2% to $188.84 billion. The company's U.S. e-commerce business is nearing breakeven excluding ad revenue, supported by supply chain improvements and lower unit costs. Walmart also expects its new $120 membership bundle combining Walmart+ and Sam's Club Plus to boost profits, while expanding delivery capacity through fulfillment centers and studying AI shopping integration.

items.summary: Walmart exceeded Q3 expectations with adjusted earnings of 65 cents per share and revenues of $188.8 billion, driven by strong e-commerce growth (17%), advertising expansion (25%), and membership gains. The company raised its fiscal 2027 guidance, projecting net sales growth of 4.9-5.2% and adjusted operating income growth of 8-8.6%. All three segments showed growth, though Sam's Club operating income declined due to prior-year comparisons and LIFO charges.

items.title: Walmart's Q3 Earnings on Deck: Is WMT Stock a Buy or Hold?
items.summary: Walmart is set to report Q3 fiscal 2027 results on November 19, with consensus estimates projecting revenues of $186.5 billion (up 3.9%) and EPS of 64 cents (up 3.2%). The Zacks model predicts an earnings beat supported by strong value demand, e-commerce growth, and higher-margin businesses. However, headwinds from pricing investments, pharmacy deflation, and elevated costs may pressure profitability. The stock trades at a premium valuation of 40.78x forward P/E.

items.title: Target vs. Walmart Stock:  Which is the Better Buy Ahead of Q3 Earnings?
items.summary: Target and Walmart are reporting Q3 earnings this week amid consumer spending concerns ahead of the holiday season. Target has significantly outperformed Walmart in 2026 (70% vs 16% YTD return) and trades at a more attractive valuation (17X forward earnings vs Walmart's 40X), while offering a higher dividend yield of 3% versus 0.8%. However, Walmart demonstrates stronger long-term performance and a more defensive business model. Target receives a Zacks Rank #2 (Buy) while Walmart gets a #3 (Hold), though investors should await Q3 results and holiday guidance before making decisions.
